A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A.1–A.8 support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v2 reports original VQA performance, retrieval ratios, efficiency measurements and boundary-identification experiments, including supplementary DeepSeek, surrogate-boundary and MMMU results.

after.justification: v3 retains the original quantitative experiments in the main text and appendices and additionally reports four qualitative model-output examples in Table 5.

M1.justification: Section 2 retains the same sampling and scoring procedure, HKB/SKB training objectives and threshold-based retrieval decisions. No algorithm step or model component changes.

E1.justification: Training and evaluation coverage remains unchanged, including MMMU in Appendix A.8. The added cases come from already evaluated Dyn-VQA (en), NoCaps and Visual7W tasks.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same No RAG, All RAG, Prompt-based and human-labeled reference comparisons and the same VLLMs. Shortening Deepseek-VL-Chat to Ds.-VL-Chat in the evaluation-consistency table is only an abbreviation.

E3.justification: Reported splits, sample counts, models, training settings, retrieval procedures and metrics remain unchanged. The added cases illustrate an existing model under existing with-retrieval and without-retrieval conditions.

E4.justification: New Section 4.4 and Table 5 add four Qwen-VL-Max cases illustrating predictions inside and outside the knowledge boundary. The efficiency, threshold-sensitivity, surrogate-boundary and appendix analyses already existed in v2.

E5.justification: Table 1 retains identical mean and standard-deviation reporting for training scores. No repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval or significance-testing information is added or revised.

E6.justification: New Table 5 reports retrieval correcting two Dyn-VQA (en) answers, while the NoCaps and Visual7W answers are marked correct both with and without retrieval. Existing numerical results, including efficiency and all appendix tables, remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, objectives and retrieval equations (1)–(8) are unchanged. Neither version adds a theorem, proof or revised derivation relative to the other.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: two boundary-identification variants, reduced retrieval while maintaining or improving VQA performance, and transfer through surrogate boundaries.

C2.justification: Section 7 newly acknowledges that the method cannot reliably distinguish visual misrecognition, including incorrect object identification and multi-view ambiguity, from knowledge gaps. This substantively qualifies the interpretation of its boundary predictions.

D1.justification: Appendices A.1, A.3 and A.4 retain the same prompts, LoRA hyperparameters, hardware, training time and API-call estimates. Code and dataset release statements are also unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 5 and the bibliography retain the same cited works and research positioning. No prior-work comparison or novelty claim is substantively revised.

P1.justification: v3 updates the analysis roadmap, inserts the case-study subsection, renumbers the held-in analysis and adds an acknowledgment. Contact information and a few grammatical expressions change; the broader narrative and section order remain stable.

P2.justification: v3 adds a full-width case table containing four images and paired answers. Figure 3 and existing tables are relocated, subsequent tables are renumbered, and the evaluation-consistency table is slightly reformatted. Existing figures retain their content.

improvement.justification: The new visual-error limitation makes the interpretation of knowledge-boundary predictions more appropriately qualified, while Table 5 provides concrete illustrations of retrieval decisions. These improve transparency and clarity, but the four illustrative cases leave the aggregate experimental evidence and reproducibility information unchanged.
